investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-14T20:06–20:07Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2) was unreachable. Because the failure occurs at the very first POST /api/agents call before any evidence can be collected, all required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway backing POST /api/agents (an AWS ELB endpoint in us-east-2) returned HTTP 502 with error code bad_gateway and message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning" for every remote-agents check in this eval run. Because the gateway failure occurs before the agent creation response is received, the runner cannot populate any required evidence fields, causing the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create to fail completely. The identical error message across all three sibling checks confirms this is a shared upstream infrastructure failure at the swarm gateway layer, not an isolated eval or runner code defect. No historical pass data is available to establish a regression baseline, and no suspect code changes are identified in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges.

investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream image generation call to be rejected with error code credit_balance_exhausted. The OpenAI API returned HTTP error type insufficient_quota / code credit_balance_exhausted before any image could be generated. As a result the stream emitted generation_error instead of generation_completed, imageUrl was never set, and both required contract assertions failed. No code defect in the eval runner or application logic is indicated by the available evidence; the failure is caused by an external billing/quota condition on the OpenAI account backing the eval credential.

The OpenAI API returned HTTP error type insufficient_quota / code credit_balance_exhausted before any image could be generated. As a result the stream emitted generation_error instead of generation_completed, imageUrl was never set, and both required contract assertions failed. No code defect in the eval runner or application logic is indicated by the available evidence; the failure is caused by an external billing/quota condition on the OpenAI account backing the eval credential.

investigations.rootCause: The AURA backend was temporarily unable to reach the upstream provider for model aura-gpt-5-5 at the time of the eval run (2026-09-14T20:06:03–16Z). The failure is scoped to the aura-gpt-5-5 provider integration at the time of this single eval run; no historical baseline exists to confirm regression, and no sibling checks corroborate a broader outage.

If GitHub Actions run history shows a successful snapshot-publishing workflow run that completed within the last 300 minutes relative to the eval time (i.e., after approximately 2026-09-14T15:07Z), it would disprove a workflow failure and point instead to a Pages deployment or CDN caching issue.

If the raw generatedAt timestamp in the live status.json is more recent than 300 minutes before the eval run time, it would indicate the snapshotAgeMinutes calculation in the runner is incorrect rather than the snapshot being genuinely stale.

If all four public-website checks (including published-observability-snapshot) had failed simultaneously, it would suggest a shared dependency failure rather than an isolated snapshot pipeline issue — but the three passing siblings rule this out.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly monitors the GitHub Actions workflow run recency for the snapshot-publishing workflow, alerting if no successful run has completed within the last 240 minutes (providing earlier warning before the 300-minute contract threshold is breached).

Add an eval that checks the raw generatedAt field in status.json against the current time independently of the snapshotAgeMinutes computed value, to detect any discrepancy between the runner's age calculation and the actual artifact timestamp.
Add an eval that verifies the GitHub Pages deployment for status.json completed successfully after each workflow run, catching cases where the workflow succeeds but the Pages publish step fails.
Consider adding a trend eval that tracks snapshotAgeMinutes over consecutive runs to detect gradual drift toward the threshold before a hard failure occurs.
